name: Presentations
lede: Open with the point, not the preamble. This pack gives you the phrases to land your evidence, guide the room, and close with an ask people can act on.
outcome: Lead with the point, make the data land, and end with an ask the room can act on.
outcomes: Open with your conclusion, so the room knows why the next ten minutes matter.
Explain a chart or number in plain English, without hiding behind jargon or caveats.
Close with a clear ask, so people leave knowing exactly what happens next.

aside.title: Built for the room, not the slide deck.
aside.body: Every line here is designed to be said out loud, at a normal pace, without notes.

words.definition: To explain something step by step so people can follow.
words.example: I’ll walk you through the three options on this slide.

words.definition: The actions that need to happen after this point.
words.example: Let’s finish with the next steps and who owns each.

words.definition: The short, bold statement that sums up your main message.
words.example: Make the headline a full sentence, not a label.

words.definition: The one idea you most want the audience to remember.
words.example: Every slide should support the same key message.

words.definition: To draw attention to the most important part of something.
words.example: I’ll highlight the two numbers that changed the forecast.

words.definition: To start examining a topic in detail, often after a summary.
words.example: Let’s dive into the numbers behind that drop.

words.definition: To look at a small part of the data more closely.
words.example: If we drill down, one region explains the whole gap.

words.definition: To step back and look at the bigger picture.
words.example: Let’s zoom out and look at the full year.

words.definition: A picture of numbers that makes a pattern easier to see.
words.example: This chart shows growth slowing in the second half.

words.definition: The general direction something is moving over time.
words.example: The trend is clear: customers want fewer options.

words.definition: A single fact or number used as evidence.
words.example: One data point isn’t enough to call it a trend.

words.definition: Facts or examples that show why your point is true.
words.example: The evidence points one way, so I’ll be direct.

words.definition: A specific case that makes an idea easier to understand.
words.example: Let me give you one example from a recent launch.

words.definition: Used to introduce a short restatement of the main points.
words.example: In summary, we solved the cost problem, not the speed.

words.definition: Used to give a short version of everything you just said.
words.example: To sum up, we need three more weeks and one hire.

words.definition: Shown on the screen for the audience to read.
words.example: On the slide you can see the full breakdown by region.

words.definition: Used to point the audience to something visible.
words.example: As you can see, the gap closes after April.

words.definition: To go on to the next topic or slide.
words.example: Let’s move on to the part everyone came for.

words.definition: Used to explain the same idea in simpler language.
words.example: In other words, we grew, but we grew badly.

words.definition: The single idea you want the audience to take away.
words.example: Make one point per slide and say it clearly.

words.definition: A statement you say is true but still need to prove.
words.example: That’s a strong claim, so let’s show the evidence.

words.definition: To support a statement with facts or examples.
words.example: Back up the headline with one clear number.

words.definition: To make an idea clearer by giving an example or picture.
words.example: This case illustrates why the old process failed.

words.definition: To return to a topic later in the presentation.
words.example: I’ll come back to that question at the end.

words.definition: To ask the audience to save questions for the end.
words.example: I’ll hold questions until we reach the final slide.

words.definition: A polite way to close a talk and invite a response.
words.example: Thank you — that brings me to the end.

words.definition: An invitation for the audience to ask what they need.
words.example: That’s the plan — any questions before we vote?

words.definition: To invite everyone in the room to speak.
words.example: I’ll open the floor for ten minutes of debate.
